title: AgentAuthorityRunManifest
description:
Everything needed to reproduce a run and to know what was actually tested.

A benchmark artifact is reproducible on its own: seeds, checksums and a frozen
fixture make the *world* recoverable. That is not sufficient for a result. A claim
like "this pattern failed to propagate revocation" is a claim about a particular
system, at a particular version, under a particular configuration, on a particular
network topology - and without those recorded, the finding is unreproducible even
though the fixture is.

This manifest exists to make findings attributable. In particular
`systems_under_test` is an array rather than a single entry, because a finding must
be assignable to a specific component or explicitly marked ambiguous. If evidence
cannot establish which component broke an authority chain, that ambiguity is itself
a reportable evidence failure, not a bookkeeping inconvenience.

Unlike the trace schemas in this directory, this file is hand-authored: no pydantic
model defines it yet. It is a proposal, versioned independently of the benchmark.

manifest_version.description: Version of this manifest schema, not of the run.

run_id.description: Stable identifier for this run, unique within the operator's records.

created_at.description: Run start. `format` is only an annotation in JSON Schema 2020-12, so the pattern is what actually enforces this.

operator.description: Who executed the run. Required in anything published.

run_layer.description:
Which control layer this run exercises, matching control-catalogue.yaml.

`core` runs score declared observations offline and need no topology.
`lab` runs execute against real systems and MUST declare topology and
authority-critical dependencies - a bypass or fail-closed finding is
meaningless without them.

controls_exercised.description: Control identifiers this run claims to exercise. A run may not claim a control whose asteria_v1_status is `absent`.

systems_under_test.description:
Every component in the authority path, each separately versioned.

Record the whole composed stack, not only the component of interest: a finding
attributed to a gateway that actually originated in its authorization server is
the most common way a report becomes unfair.

authority_critical_dependencies.description:
Components whose failure should deny sensitive actions (see SW-AA-L05).
Declared per architecture and before the run, so fail-closed behaviour is
testable rather than asserted.

declared_bounds.description:
Thresholds fixed BEFORE execution. A bound chosen after seeing the
measurement is not a bound (see SW-AA-L06).

conflicts_declared.description:
Relationships that a reader might reasonably think could bias the result:
authorship of an adapter or reference implementation, commercial interest in a
component, prior engagement with a vendor. Disclose in the manifest rather than
leaving it to be discovered.

limitations.description:
Known reasons this run understates or overstates behaviour. Anything dropped,
sampled, capped or skipped belongs here - silent truncation reads as coverage.

then.description: Lab runs cannot be interpreted without reachability and dependency declarations.

benchmarkIdentity.description: Which world was used. Exactly one of `frozen` or `generated`.

oneOf.description:
A generated world. These fields are the benchmark identity: the tuple that
determines the artifacts. Build provenance is recorded separately, because
the same identity only reproduces byte-identically inside the same locked
environment - seed and configuration alone do not guarantee it across
future interpreter or serializer releases.

configuration.description: The explicit configuration, or a digest of it plus a retrievable location.

buildProvenance.description:
What software produced the artifacts. Distinct from benchmark identity: this is
what makes byte-identical reproduction achievable, and it is the part that
changes when a dependency is upgraded.

synthworld_ref.description: Exact commit SHA or released version.

authored_by_benchmark_maintainer.description:
True when the benchmark maintainer wrote the adapter. Not disqualifying -
someone has to write the first one - but it changes what the result can be
cited for, so it is recorded rather than inferred.

is_reference_implementation.description:
True for a stand-in written for the benchmark rather than a shipped product.
Findings against a reference implementation are evidence about that
implementation, never about the pattern it illustrates.

topology.description:
Network facts the result depends on. Required for lab runs (SW-AA-L03): keeping
a credential away from an agent does not keep authority away from it if the agent
retains a path to the target, so reachability must be a declared fact rather than
an assumption.

agent_can_reach_target_directly.description: Whether a direct agent-to-target path existed during the run.

enforcement_points.description: Every point at which authority was enforced. More than one is normal, and an empty array is a legitimate declaration - a bearer-credential deployment genuinely has none, and forcing a value there would make the honest answer unsayable.

review.description:
Whether the party responsible for a system under test accepts the configuration
as representative. A comparative or pattern-level claim requires this; a
conformance case study does not, but should say so.
